summary: Landing review of 98b1ffe..2adf0ff (code frozen at tested commit a16bf94; a16bf94..2adf0ff touches only docs/autopilot evidence and the run record). Evidence integrity: verify-evidence.sh on a git-archive snapshot of the head's docs/autopilot/evidence-2026-10-24 reports 'verified: 127 evidence file(s)'; the cited files gate-landing.md, gate-base-r3.md, mutant-c1a-invert-ledger-r2.md, mutant-c2-numeric-range-r2.md, mutant-c2-auto-style-r2.md, mutant-c4-resume-guard-r2.md, mutant-c7-header-check-r2.md, mutant-c6-no-entry-ok.md and mutant-c7-exists-guard.md were verified by name (9 verified). gate-landing.md records tested commit a16bf94, sandbox bwrap, network denied, all 10 commands exit 0 with the counts the record claims. No tracked file was deleted, docs/autopilot.md and the policy JSON are unchanged from base, and nothing was pushed. I reviewed C7 (import_litsearch.py: refusals run before any write, staged rename, rollback on append failure or audit rejection; the validate_search_log refactor matches the old behaviour), C6 (proofread.ts sha256 identity, the merge wiring, generate-slides record_generated), C4 (sampling.py and the cli guards) and C5 (deckTypeAudit), and found nothing material in them. One blocking gap is in C1(a). check_paper's METRIC_RE has an ASCII-alphanumeric negative lookahead and a '.' negative lookbehind, so any decimal written with a unit attached (12.5ms, 3.5mm, 1.5M, 2.5x), any APA leading-zero-free decimal (r = .85, p < .001) and a percent written as '95%CI' are never extracted. The draft passes with exit 0 even when the ledger lacks those numbers. I confirmed this by running a copied regex on its own; no project code was run. INDEPENDENT MUTATION TARGETS (selected by this reviewer, landing r1): C1 — integrity_gate.py split_body `heading_level(line) <= refs_level` -> `heading_level(line) < refs_level`; failure to catch: an untraced decimal in an '## Appendix' that follows '## References' at the same level must still produce number-not-in-ledger and exit 1. C1(a) extra — integrity_gate.py METRIC_RE decimal alternative `(\d+\.\d+)` -> `(\d+\.\d{2,})`; detector: an untraced one-decimal value ('12.5') must exit 1. C2 — integrity_gate.py APA_PART_RE drop the `\s+et al\.?` alternative; detector: '(Smith et al., 2020)' with no References entry must be named citation-without-entry, exit 1. C3 — append one trailing space or newline to research-proposal/scripts/integrity_gate.py only; detector: tests/test_vendored_gate_core.py must fail. C4 — sampling.py `random.Random(seed).sample(range(len(records)), limit)` -> `range(len(records) - 1)` (the last record can never be drawn); detector: a seeded fixture whose expected sample includes the final in-window record. C5 — qa.mjs appendix filter `s.layout !== "section" && !CLOSING_RE...` -> `!CLOSING_RE...` (section dividers count as appendix slides); detector: a defense deck whose 'Backup' divider is followed only by another section divider must still emit P2 missing-backup. C6 — proofread.ts `STATUSES.has(entry.status ?? "")` -> `entry.status !== undefined`; detector: a proofread.json entry with a matching sha256 but status 'todo' must make merge-to-pptx/merge-to-pdf exit non-zero and name the slide. C7 — import_litsearch.py `if f"row {new_index} " in p` -> `f"row {new_index - 1} "`; detector: an import whose new row the audit rejects (e.g. an export path made non-project-owned) must exit 2 and leave neither the export dir nor a modified search_log.csv, including when the log already holds a valid earlier row.

findings.title: C1(a) number gate misses decimals with attached units, leading-dot decimals and '95%CI'
findings.what_goes_wrong: METRIC_RE = (?<![A-Za-z0-9_.])(?:[nN]\s*=\s*(\d[\d,]*)|(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*%|(\d+\.\d+))(?![A-Za-z0-9_]). The trailing lookahead rejects a decimal followed directly by a letter, and backtracking cannot rescue it. The leading lookbehind rejects a digit preceded by '.'. As a result 'latency 12.5ms', '3.5mm slices', '1.5M parameters', 'a 2.5x speedup', 'r = .85', 'p < .001' and '95%CI' produce no metric_numbers at all. check_numbers never compares them with the ledger, and check_paper exits 0 even though the ledger lacks those values. C1(a) requires exit 1 and the offending item named for 'a metric-like number in the draft prose (decimal, percentage …) absent from the ledger's value column'.
findings.why_vulnerable: The results ledger stores the number and the unit separately (the test LEDGER header has value,unit,dispersion columns), so drafts naturally render a value with its unit. Unit-glued decimals (ms, mm, M/B, x) are routine in the CS and medical-imaging papers this skill targets. APA style requires dropping the leading zero for r and p, so '.85' and '.001' are standard forms too. These are exactly the fabricated-number shapes the gate exists to catch. The tests (test_untraced_decimal_fails_and_is_named, the Chinese-prose, CI-in-brackets and thousands-separator tests) only use space-separated or CJK-adjacent decimals, so the suite never exercises the boundary. The recorded mutants target the comparison and the stripping logic, not METRIC_RE's lookarounds.
findings.how_to_confirm: Write a draft line 'Inference took 12.5ms and r = .85.' with a ledger that contains neither value, plus a valid bib and checklist, and run check_paper.py; expect exit 0 with no number-not-in-ledger. Without running project code, I ran the copied regex on its own with python3 -I: finditer returns [] for '12.5ms', 'r = .85', 'p < .001', '2.5x', '3.5mm', '1.5M' and '95%CI', and ['0.87', '12.5'] for 'Dice 0.87 and 12.5 ms'.
findings.recommendation: Drop the alphabetic part of the trailing lookahead for the decimal and percent alternatives, e.g. (?![0-9_]) or (?!\d). Allow a leading-dot decimal with (?<![A-Za-z0-9_])(?:0?\.\d+) and normalize '.85' and '0.85' to the same key in normalize_number. Add regression tests for '12.5ms', '3.5 mm', 'r = .85', 'p < .001', '2.5x' and '95%CI'. Because the core is vendored, mirror the change into research-proposal/scripts/integrity_gate.py byte for byte and re-run the C1 mutants.

limits: Reviewer is a fresh-context Claude subagent, the same model family as the author, so it is not independent in the sense the contract's Codex reviewer would be. I inspected only the pinned head via git show/diff/archive and ran no project code or tests; the one behavioural check was a copied METRIC_RE regex run on its own with python3 -I. I did not re-run the machine gate or any mutant and relied on hash-verified saved evidence for gate results and KILLED statuses; I did not open every mutant evidence file, only spot-checked those named above. Not deeply reviewed: check_proposal.py's exemption and style-dispatch logic beyond the shared core, the test files' assertions line by line, merge-to-pdf.ts (assumed symmetric with merge-to-pptx.ts), the docs-only SKILL.md/README/learnings changes, scholar-slides qa_report.mjs wiring, and the lit-search jev path beyond the diff. No live API, network, Gemini or bun paths were exercised.
